description:
Moderator pings are a system that allow members to quickly and easily get the attention of moderators for whatever reason is necessary.

During a mod ping, Wynem will ping three members of the lowest ranking moderator role, with 60 seconds between each ping. If no moderator has responded, it will ping the entire role. If still no one has responded, it repeats this process two more times with the next two higher tiers of moderator role.

When picking which members to ping, Wynem prioritises members who are online, then on do not disturb, then idle, then offline.

description: As well as the command, mod pings can be triggered by mentioning any role named <@&Modping> or <@&Moderator Ping>. Capitalisation and spaces in the role name do not matter, so names like <@&ModPing> and <@&moderatorping> work too.
By default, the moderator role tiers are guessed, and Wynem will use the three highest moderator roles in the server. A moderator role is any role that has at least one of these permissions:

rows: Can delete messages sent by other members
Can kick members from the server
Can ban members from the server

description: If the guessed roles don't fit your server, you can manually set up to three custom roles to be used instead with the <command:setmodpingroles [role] [role2] [role3]|serverconfig modpingroles set role:[role] role2:[role2] role3:[role3]> command.

tabs.name: Triggering a mod ping
content: To trigger a mod ping, use the <command:modping|modping> command. Wynem will start pinging moderators one at a time. Only one mod ping can be running in a channel at a time.

content: A moderator can resolve the mod ping by pressing the `Resolve` button, or by simply sending a message in the channel.
If you started the mod ping, you can press the `Cancel` button to stop it.
If anyone who is not a moderator presses the `Resolve` button, they will get an error that only they can see.

content: If there is nobody that can be pinged, Wynem will respond with `There is no one available to moderator ping`. If every tier has been pinged and no moderator has responded, Wynem gives up on the mod ping.

tabs.name: Toggling mod pings
content: Mod pings are enabled by default. To toggle whether members can trigger them, use the <command:togglemodping|serverconfig toggle modping> command. This requires the `Manage Guild` permission.

content: Running the command again re-enables them.

content: While mod pings are disabled, trying to trigger one will show an error.

tabs.name: Setting the mod ping roles
content: To set custom moderator ping roles, use the <command:setmodpingroles [role] [role2] [role3]|serverconfig modpingroles set role:[role] role2:[role2] role3:[role3]> command, providing up to three roles. This requires the `Manage Guild` permission.
The order of the roles is the order of priority, so the first role is the tier that gets pinged first. Running the command again will overwrite any previously set roles.
For example: <command:setmodpingroles @Helpers @Moderators @Admins|serverconfig modpingroles set role:@Helpers role2:@Moderators role3:@Admins>

content: Every role you provide must be a moderator role. If one of them isn't, you will get an error instead.

tabs.name: Viewing the mod ping roles
content: To view the currently set moderator ping roles, use the <command:viewmodpingroles|serverconfig modpingroles view> command. This requires the `Manage Guild` permission.

content: If there are no custom roles set, you will be told that Wynem is using the guessed roles instead.

data.title: No moderator ping roles set

tabs.name: Removing the mod ping roles
content: To remove the custom moderator ping roles and go back to the guessed roles, run the <command:setmodpingroles|serverconfig modpingroles set> command without providing any roles.
You will be prompted to confirm that you want to remove the roles. Press remove to continue.
